title: Senior Tax Analyst, Corporate Tax
description:
Where Conviviality is at work.

Pernod Ricard is a global premium international champagnes and spirits company. We’re the team behind leading brands such as ABSOLUT® Vodka, Jameson® Irish Whiskey, Malibu®, Kahlúa® Liqueur, The Glenlivet®, Beefeater and Malfy Gins, and a leading portfolio of American whiskey brands including Jefferson’s, Rabbit Hole, TX, Smooth Ambler and Skrewball™ whiskey.

Working at Pernod Ricard is all about igniting conviviality in all that we do. Derived from the French word, convivialité…it means human connection, authenticity, friendly, and jovial. Conviviality is energy and spirit with a splash of je ne sais quoi and is a core philosophy around how we live and work at Pernod Ricard.

  

Guided by our 4 core values: (1) grounded in the real; (2) fiercely authentic; (3) passion for challenge; and (4) connected beyond borders; we are team players, dream makers, trailblazers, movers and (cocktail) shakers. We have a passion for living life to the fullest, making new friends every day, and realizing our potential as people and as a business!

The salary range for this role, based in New York, is $91,300.00 to $125,598.00. The range may vary if the role outside of this location. Base salaries are determined during our interview process, by assessing a candidate’s experience, skills against internal peers and against the scope and responsibilities of the position.

**Job Summary:**

Join Pernod Ricard's U.S. Tax team and play a critical role in supporting tax compliance, reporting, and planning activities across a dynamic portfolio of domestic and international entities. Reporting to the Tax Director, this role offers broad exposure to corporate income tax, tax accounting, audits, transfer pricing, and strategic tax initiatives. This is an exciting opportunity for a tax professional who enjoys solving complex challenges, partnering across functions, and contributing to a high-performing finance organization.

**Who will love this job:**

You will thrive in this role if you:

* Enjoy navigating complex tax regulations and translating technical concepts into business insights.
* Have a strong attention to detail and take pride in delivering accurate, high-quality work.
* Are naturally curious and stay informed on evolving tax laws and regulatory developments.
* Enjoy partnering with stakeholders across finance, accounting, FP&A, and international teams.
* Take ownership of your work and can successfully manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
* Are motivated by continuous learning, process improvement, and finding more efficient ways to work.

**What you’ll do**:

  

* Prepare federal income tax and non-income tax filings.
* Review state and local income tax returns to ensure accuracy and compliance.
* Support quarterly and year-end tax provision processes, including forecast reporting and IFRIC 23 requirements.
* Prepare monthly tax account reconciliations and analyze tax-related balances.
* Respond to notices and inquiries from federal, state, and local taxing authorities.
* Assist with federal and state tax audits and support requests from auditors.
* Manage and monitor tax filing calendars to ensure timely compliance with all filing obligations.
* Conduct tax research and contribute to tax planning initiatives and transfer pricing analyses.
* Partner closely with Finance, Accounting, FP&A, affiliates, and global tax teams on tax-related matters.
* Monitor technical tax developments and assess potential impacts on the business.
* Participate in special projects and continuous improvement initiatives that enhance tax processes and controls.

**What’s in it for me?**

Being part of an inclusive and diverse company where professional development and internal career mobility is front-and-center to our talent strategy. This means your career at Pernod Ricard has many possibilities. You'll be part of a culture that celebrates the rich diversity of our people across the globe and be part of our long-standing commitment to making exceptional products, giving back to our communities, and honoring our responsibility to preserve the environment.

**Required qualifications**:

* Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Taxation, or a related field.
* CPA designation required.
* Minimum of 3 years of experience within a Big 4 or well-regarded public accounting firm focused on corporate tax compliance and reporting.
* Strong knowledge of U.S. corporate income tax law, state and local taxation, and international tax concepts.
* Experience preparing and reviewing corporate income tax returns and related tax accounting under ASC 740 and/or IAS 12.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, ONESOURCE, and Bloomberg Tax.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret complex information and deliver actionable insights.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Ability to work independently while effectively collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders.
* Continuous improvement mindset with a passion for learning and process enhancement.

**Target Hire Date****:**

2026-12-14

When you join Pernod Ricard, you’ll experience a workplace that is rich in heritage, driven by our iconic brands and a long-standing commitment to sustainability, safety, and giving back to the people and communities where we work. We know that happiness at work starts with that feeling of belonging you get from an inclusive culture where being uniquely you is celebrated. Our values are lived, they drive our behaviors, and it’s what brings our culture to life.

  

Our work philosophy celebrates the magic of human connection with the flexibility needed to provide one's most meaningful contribution. We offer a flexible work policy, with most of our positions offering a a hybrid option with flexibility to work remotely 2 days a week. As a global employer, we understand that not everyone’s working hours are the same, and we empower our employees to work the hours that make the most sense for them and their team’s schedules.

  

We offer employees great benefits and perks to toast to a life filled with support. Check out PRUSABenefits.com for details.

title: Financial Analyst
description:

The Financial Analyst partners closely with Expense Management, Product, Pricing, and senior leadership to deliver actionable insights, enhance expense transparency, and support business decision-making. title: FP&A Analyst - Car Rental Business
description:
**Driven to be the Best**

**People. Performance. Purpose.**

At Avis Budget Group, we’re driven to be the best vehicle rental company in the world, together. Our 25,000 employees raise the bar every day, bringing different perspectives, taking ownership, and leading with integrity. We’re defining the future of mobility with safe, sustainable solutions that move people, businesses, and communities forward.

We're looking for an **FP&A Analyst** to join the team supporting financial reporting and performance analysis across our rental business segments. This role sits at the intersection of Sales and Finance — translating commercial performance into financial results and helping the business understand why the numbers move the way they do. The core focus of this role is supporting the ongoing development of our profit allocation tool.

**What You'll Do:**

  

* Prepare recurring and ad hoc reporting on business segment performance (e.g., corporate accounts, channels, geographies, rate/mix)
* Analyze P&L results against sales plans, forecast, and prior year; identify and explain key drivers of variance
* Support the Sales–Finance link by translating account/segment performance trends into financial terms sales leaders can act on, and vice versa
* Assist in building out and maintaining the revenue and cost allocation tool — including logic for attributing P&L cost lines down to the rental agreement level, and applying driver-based allocation methods for costs that can't be directly attributed
* Partner with IT, Risk, and other Finance teams to gather requirements, test logic, and validate outputs as the allocation tool evolves
* Pull and manipulate data from internal systems (Oracle/OCI, Redshift, etc.) using SQL; build and maintain models/reporting in Excel
* Support month-end closing and reporting cycles with accurate, timely deliverables
* Step in to support the wider Commercial Finance team on ad hoc projects and priority requests
* Continuously looking for ways to improve reporting efficiency and data quality

**Perks You’ll Get:**

  

* Access to Medical, Dental, Vision, Life and Disability insurance
* Eligible to elect other voluntary benefits including: Group Auto Insurance, Group Home Insurance, Pet Insurance, Legal Assistance, Identity Theft Protection, FSA, Accident Insurance, Critical Illness Insurance, and additional life insurance coverages
* 401(k) Retirement Plan with company matched contributions
* Full training to learn the business and enhance professional skills
* Employee discounts, including discounted prices on the purchase of Avis/Budget cars
* Access to an Employee Assistance Program for services including counseling, financial and legal consultation, referrals for care service and more

**What We're Looking For:**

  

* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills — comfortable digging into data to find the "why"
* Working knowledge of P&L structure and financial analysis fundamentals
* Clear written and verbal communication skills; able to work cross-functionally
* Proficiency in Microsoft Excel; comfort with the broader Microsoft Office suite
* SQL/Python proficiency a strong plus
* Familiarity with applying AI/automation tools to reporting and analysis workflows is a plus
* A genuine curiosity and enthusiasm for the business, not just the numbers
* Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics, or related field (or equivalent experience)

The annual starting salary for this position is between $65,000 – $80,000 annually. Factors that may affect starting pay within this range include geography/market, skills, education, experience, and other qualifications of the successful candidate.

**Who We Are:**

Here at Avis Budget Group, you will be joining a team of 25,000 driven people, performing with purpose. Together, we’re moving the future of transportation forward with our innovative, customer-focused solutions.

Our culture is performance driven, where we encourage and support each other to be at our best through leadership, training, tools, and rewards.

We are proud to make a positive difference to the lives of our colleagues, customers, and communities where we operate.

This advertisement does not constitute a promise or guarantee of employment. This advertisement describes the general nature and level of this position only. Essential functions and responsibilities may change as business needs require. The compensation and benefits information is accurate as of the date of this posting. title: Corporate Controller
description:
### **VSA's purpose is to design for a better human experience. As a strategy and design agency, we blend consumer insights and data with human-centered design to activate meaningful, motivating and measurable experiences in an increasingly noisy world. With offices in Chicago, New York and San Francisco, VSA offers a full range of fully integrated capabilities—branding, advertising, data science and technology—all under one roof. VSA is also a proud member of Meet The People, an international family of unified and independent agencies. For more than 40 years, we have delivered solutions for business and creative leaders at some of the world's most respected brands and forward-thinking organizations, including Google, Nike and IBM.**

**Open role in MTP Office locations, including New York, and Chicago**

**Visa Sponsorship** is not available for this position, now or in the future. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States on a permanent basis without requiring employer sponsorship.

  

**Role Overview**

The Corporate Controller owns accounting, consolidation, and financial reporting for Meet The People's 13 legal entities across the United States and Canada. This role produces one accurate, timely set of consolidated financials from a multi-entity, multi-currency group, and owns the close, internal controls, and the external audit. As the group's corporate accounting lead, the Controller sets the accounting policies, close standards, and controls that every pillar and entity finance team follows.

The Controller will also serve as interim head of finance for one of MTP's agencies, spending roughly 30–40% of their time running that agency's finance function and developing its Director of Finance to take on the full role.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities** (Other duties may be assigned)

**Consolidation and Multi-entity Accounting**

* Consolidate all 13 US and Canadian entities into accurate, timely consolidated financial statements under US GAAP.
* Run intercompany accounting, including transactions, cross-charges, reconciliations, and elimination entries across all entities.
* Maintain a consistent chart of accounts, accounting policies, and close procedures across every entity.
* Set group-wide close calendars, reporting packages, and review standards for pillar and entity finance teams, and review their submissions before consolidation.
* Build scalable consolidation processes and tools that can absorb new entities as MTP grows.

**Close and Financial Reporting**

* Run the monthly, quarterly, and annual close for all entities on a defined, predictable calendar.
* Prepare consolidated and entity-level financial statements, including P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow.
* Oversee transactional accounting across entities; own balance sheet integrity, including intercompany transaction reconciliations.
* Partner with operations, HR, and IT so transactional data flows cleanly and accurately into the accounting records.
* Provide the CFO and leadership with accurate actuals, account analysis, and variance explanations for management reporting.

**Internal Controls and Accounting Policy**

* Establish, document, and maintain accounting policies, procedures, and internal controls.
* Own the internal control environment and risk assessment over financial reporting.
* Oversee technical accounting, including revenue recognition (ASC 606), leases (ASC 842), and business combinations (ASC 805).

**Audit and Tax**

* Coordinate the annual external audit and act as the auditors' primary day-to-day contact; resolve audit findings and implement corrective actions promptly.
* Coordinate US and Canadian tax compliance with external tax advisors, including income tax, sales tax, GST/HST, and 1099 information reporting.
* Support the CFO on tax planning and in relationships with tax advisors, banks, and other financial partners.

**Acquisitions and Integration**

* Support financial due diligence for acquisitions if needed, focusing on the quality of the target's accounting, controls, and close.

-----------------

DeepMind is building frontier financial reasoning and agentic capabilities across Gemini and our enterprise agent harnesses. Moving AI from a generalist research assistant to an agent that can autonomously complete financial workflows requiresmore than raw pre-training scale - it requires deep domain mechanics embedded directly into how models are post-trained, how agent harnesses and tools are architected, and how evaluations measure real-world finance.

As a Finance Subject Matter Experts (SME), you will work with models, evaluations, and post-training data in the following three Finance domains -

* Quantitative Trading
* Corporate Finance - specifically with experience across FP&A, Audit and Tax
* Alternative Asset Management

Unlike traditional advisory roles that stop at high-level feedback or static prompt writing, you will sit directly in the model development loop alongside Research Scientists, Post-Training Engineers, and Product Managers. You will prioritize differentiated financial workflows, design end-to-end financial benchmarks, construct atomic and deterministic grading rubrics, diagnose multi-step agent trajectories, repair near-miss model reasoning traces, design verifiable reward signals, and co-build domain-specific agent skills.

Artificial intelligence will be one of humanity’s most transformative inventions. At Google DeepMind, we are a pioneering AI lab with exceptional interdisciplinary teams focused on advancing AI development to solve complex global challenges and accelerate high-quality product innovation for billions of users. You will join at a point where the finance function is moving from reporting-focused controlling towards forward-looking planning and analysis. This is a hands-on role with high visibility: you will work directly with business unit leads and Group Accounting, and you will have real influence over how performance is measured and understood across the group.

  

**What You Will Do**

* **Own the business unit P&L, end to end**

* **Support the month-end close**

  + Reconcile ledger data to consolidated actuals and resolve differences before reporting
  + Produce variance analysis (month-on-month, budget-versus-actual, year-on-year) with clear root-cause commentary traceable to source data

* **Present the numbers to stakeholders**
  + Present monthly performance to business unit leads and Group leadership
  + Translate financial movements into a clear business narrative rather than a list of variances
  + Own the recurring reporting pack for your business units and stand behind the detail
* **Drive budgeting, forecasting and modelling**
  + Run the annual budget and rolling forecast cycles for your business units together with operational stakeholders, in support of the Director of FP&A
  + Build and maintain driver-based financial models at the appropriate level of detail
  + Track forecast accuracy over time and explain deviations
  + Support ad-hoc modelling: scenario analysis, business cases, and margin and profitability deep dives

* The ability to present to, and constructively challenge, senior non-finance stakeholders
* Structured, accuracy-focused working style and the ability to meet close deadlines
* Fluent business English

* Hands-on experience with LucaNet and NetSuite
* Working knowledge of IFRS in a consolidated group

description:

The Director of Financial Reporting & Technical Accounting is responsible for overseeing the company's internal and external financial reporting, technical accounting, and employee benefit plan accounting functions, including pension, other post retirement benefits and 401(k) plan accounting. This role will serve as a strategic partner to senior finance leadership, ensuring the accuracy and integrity of financial statements, compliance with US GAAP and IFRS reporting requirements, and the timely resolution of complex accounting matters and proper accounting and disclosure of the company's employee benefit obligations. The ideal candidate brings deep technical accounting expertise, strong research and documentation skills, and a forward-thinking mindset toward digital innovation and process transformation.

**Primary Duties/Responsibilities:**

* Provide day-to-day leadership, direction, and oversight to the Financial Reporting and Technical Accounting teams, ensuring accurate and timely execution of all activities.
* Coordinate with external actuaries to obtain annual actuarial valuations, review key assumptions (discount rate, expected return on plan assets, mortality tables), and ensure proper reflection of valuation results in the financial statements.
* Communicate with plan asset managers to obtain year-end plan asset information, review investment performance, and ensure proper classification and disclosure of plan assets in accordance with the fair value hierarchy.
* Oversee the preparation and review of annual 401(k) plan financial statements.
* Review and approve balance sheet account reconciliations, including pension and benefit plan-related accounts, ensuring all reconciling items are properly documented and resolved within established timelines.
* Serve as a primary resource for accounting guidance on day-to-day transactions and emerging accounting issues raised by business units and finance partners.
* Respond to inquiries from internal stakeholders regarding the application of accounting policies and standards.
* Oversee the preparation and review of monthly financial statements and management reporting packages, ensuring accuracy and completeness.
* Lead the preparation and review of annual financial statements and footnote disclosures in accordance with US GAAP.
* Oversee the implementation of new accounting standards (ASUs, IFRS updates), including impact assessments, policy updates, and communication to relevant stakeholders.
* Prepare and maintain accounting policy documentation, ensuring policies are current, comprehensive, and aligned with applicable accounting standards.
* Research and document the accounting treatment for complex, non-routine, or judgmental transactions, including mergers and acquisitions, new contracts, financing arrangements, and other significant business events, through the preparation of formal technical accounting memoranda.
* Support special projects and ad hoc analyses as requested by senior finance leadership.
* Support internal control self-assessment of the financial closing process.
* Conduct periodic performance reviews for direct reports, establish individual development plans, and identify training and growth opportunities to build team capabilities.

This position description is intended for the purpose of position evaluation and salary positioning and is not a contract setting forth the full scope of employment. The employer retains the right to deviate from the description at its discretion, without notice.

**Education/Experience/Background:**

* Bachelor’s degree desired in Accounting, Finance or related field.
* Masters in Business Administration or CPA license is a plus.
* 8 to 12 years of progressive experience in accounting, financial reporting and technical accounting.
* Demonstrated experience managing external financial reporting processes in a multi-entity environment under both US GAAP and IFRS.
* Proven ability to perform complex accounting research and document conclusions in well-structured technical accounting memoranda.
* Proven ability to lead, develop, and retain high-performing teams.
* Experience with the preparation and review of financial statements, footnote disclosures, and supporting schedules.
* Knowledge and Expertise in:
  + US Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) requirements.
  + IFRS accounting requirements.
  + Technical accounting research and application of new and existing accounting standards.

**Knowledge/Skills/Abilities:**

* Strong technical knowledge of US GAAP and IFRS, including the ability to research, interpret, and apply complex accounting standards.
* Demonstrated ability to write clear, concise, and well-supported technical accounting memoranda on complex accounting issues.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex financial and accounting information to executive leadership and non-financial stakeholders in a clear and articulate manner.
* Ability to effectively communicate and collaborate with external actuaries and plan asset managers to obtain, review, and validate key inputs for pension and benefit plan accounting.
* Strong understanding of internal controls and the ability to identify risks and key controls within the financial reporting process.
* Ability to lead and/or support finance transformation and process improvement projects.
* Ability to align financial reporting operations with broader organizational goals and drive long-term value.
* Ability to build strong relationships with and deliver value to stakeholders through communication and collaboration.

Preferred:

* Big 4 public accounting experience.

**Purpose of Position:**

The C&I Portfolio Manager/Team Lead, is responsible for senior-level oversight of the risk management and performance of the Bank’s commercial and industrial portfolio, including nonprofit, CDFI, for-profit, owner-occupied mortgage financing and other mission-aligned and commercial borrowers. This role serves as a senior credit and personnel leader, exercising independent credit judgement on complex relationships, managing and developing portfolio management staff, and ensuring portfolio practices align with the Bank’s risk appetite and regulatory expectations.

In addition to overseeing a portfolio of the most complex or high-risk relationships, this role leads the C&I portfolio management team and is responsible for identifying emerging risks, strengthening portfolio management practices, improving tools and processes, and representing the C&I PM function in internal governance, audit, and regulatory contexts.

The position requires advanced C&I credit expertise, demonstrated experience managing teams and diverse loan portfolios, strong judgement, leadership capability, and the ability to work independently and influence outcomes across multiple stakeholders.

**Essential Job Functions:**

Senior Portfolio Oversight and Risk Leadership

* Provide senior-level oversight of portfolio risk, performance trends, and emerging issues across the C&I portfolio, including nonprofit, for-profit, CDFI, and other commercial and mission-aligned borrowers.
* Independently evaluate complex credits, higher risk relationships, and non-routine structures.
* Review, challenge, and approve complex credit recommendations, risk ratings, and exception requests.
* Serve as a senior escalation point for portfolio issues, including criticized assets and problem credits.
* Lead strategy development for risk mitigation, remediation plans, and workout approaches where necessary.
* Ensure portfolio management practices are consistent with Bank policy, regulatory guidance, and best practices.

Credit Expertise and Decision Influence

* Provide expert guidance on loan structures, covenant frameworks, and risk identification.
* Challenge assumptions in underwriting and portfolio management to strengthen overall credit quality.
* Contribute to policy interpretation and recommend enhancements to credit standards where appropriate.
* Represent the C&I Portfolio Management perspective in internal credit committees, governance forums, audits, and examinations.
* Perform independent research and analysis on industry developments and trends.

Leadership and Talent Development

* Lead, mentor, and provide technical guidance to AVP/VP-level portfolio managers and other team members.
* Review work product for quality, consistency, and sound credit judgement.
* Set clear performance expectations, allocate work effectively, and support staff development through timely feedback and coaching.
* Promote strong collaboration, accountability, and professional standards across the team.

Process Improvement and Strategic Contribution

* Identify opportunities to enhance portfolio management tools, reporting, and workflows.
* Partner with internal stakeholders (Credit Risk, Compliance, Technology, etc.) to improve systems and data integrity.
* Contribute to broader strategic initiatives related to C&I portfolio risk management, reporting, and growth.
* Perform other duties as assigned, including involvement in complex new originations.

**Knowledge, Skills and Experience Requirements:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, or related field, or equivalent advanced commercial credit experience; advanced degree or professional certification (MBA, CRC, CFA, CPA) preferred.
* 10+ years of progressively responsible experience in commercial banking and C&I portfolio management, including significant experience with nonprofit, for-profit, CDFI, owner-occupied mortgage financing, and other commercial borrowers.
* Demonstrated expertise in C&I credit structures, cash-flow and collateral analysis, covenant design, risk rating, and portfolio monitoring across diverse industries and borrower types.
* Proven ability to exercise independent credit judgement on complex, higher-risk, or non-routine transactions.
* Experience reviewing and challenging credit work prepared by others, including risk ratings, covenant structures, and exception requests.
* Experience managing criticized assets, workout situations, or remediation plans.
* Strong understanding of bank regulatory expectations, loan policy frameworks, and risk governance practices.
* Proven ability to influence outcomes across relationship managers, underwriters, credit administration, and senior stakeholders.
* Demonstrated experience formally managing portfolio management or credit professionals, including work allocation, coaching, performance management, and talent development.
* Demonstrated ability to identify systemic risks, recommend process improvements, and contribute to portfolio-level strategy.
* Firm understanding of Federal/State Regulations including but not limited to EOCA, Regulation B, CRA and NYDFS Rule 76.
* Advanced written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex credit concepts to senior audiences.
* High proficiency in financial analysis tools, data interpretation, and portfolio reporting.
* Familiarity with Salesforce, Moody’s CreditLens, and Tableau preferred.

title: Legal counsel, US
description:
At Bending Spoons, we’re striving to build one of the all-time great companies. A company that serves a huge number of customers. A company where team members grow to their full potential. A company that functions at unparalleled levels of effectiveness and efficiency. A company that creates value for shareowners at an extraordinary rate. And a company that does so while adhering to high ethical standards.
  
  
In pursuit of this objective, we acquire and improve digital businesses, not to sell on, but to own and operate for the long term. The transformations we make are often deep—designed to speed up innovation, benefit customers, and strengthen business performance. Here, hierarchy is minimal and teams are small and talent-dense. We operate established products with the ambition, agility, and urgency of a startup. Across the company, we integrate AI deeply into how we work so that human judgment and machine intelligence reinforce each other.
  
  
For a talented, driven, and collaborative individual, working at Bending Spoons is an opportunity to learn, make an impact, and progress their career at an exceptionally high rate. That’s our promise to such a candidate.

**A few examples of your responsibilities**
-------------------------------------------

* **Support our acquisitions.** Support and advise our Accounting, Finance, and Business Acquisitions team on cross-border acquisitions, conducting due diligence, analysing and drafting transaction documents, and following post-completion integrations.
* **Draft and negotiate contracts.** Handle cross-border commercial contracts with vendors and customers—initial drafting and review of confidentiality, consulting, licensing, SaaS, and other technology-related agreements, while applying your judgment to validate terms and manage risk.
* **Support product launches.** Partner with product teams on global launches by drafting external communications, legal terms, and policies—leveraging AI to produce first drafts efficiently and focusing your expertise on accuracy, compliance, and strategic alignment.
* **Advise across the business.** Partner cross-functionally and collaborate with outside counsel to deliver practical legal advice and risk mitigation strategies on a broad range of topics—including technology, product, marketing, commercial and regulatory matters, intellectual property, consumer protection, and AI governance.
* **Manage disputes.** Handle disputes and litigation in the US and abroad, coordinating with external advisers and ensuring alignment across business functions.
* **Build scalable legal tools.** Create and maintain forms, playbooks, and other scalable tools—integrating AI-powered workflows to support the company’s high-growth business.
* **Stay ahead of regulation.** Monitor legal and regulatory developments and proactively identify opportunities to unlock value and address evolving business needs.

**What we look for**
--------------------

* Reasoning ability. Given the necessary knowledge, you can solve complex problems. You think from first principles, and structure your ideas sharply. You resist the influence of biases. You identify and take care of the details that matter.
* Drive. You’re extremely ambitious in everything you do—and your initiative, effort, and tenacity match the intensity of your ambition. You feel deeply responsible for your work. You hold yourself to a high—and rising—bar.
* Team spirit. You give generously and without the expectation of receiving in return. You support the best idea, not your idea. You're always happy to get your hands dirty to help your team. You’re reliable, honest, and transparent.
* Proficiency in English. You read, write, and speak proficiently in English.
* Some experience. After obtaining a law degree, you practiced at a law firm or as in-house counsel for a period of time, in which you encountered some of the main challenges you’ll face in the role.

**What we offer**
-----------------

* Incredibly talented, entrepreneurial teams. You’ll work in small, result-oriented, autonomous teams alongside some of the brightest people in your field.
* An exceptional opportunity for growth. We go to great lengths to hire individuals of outstanding potential—then, our priority is to put them in the ideal position to thrive. Spooners in their 20s lead products worth hundreds of millions of dollars. And if you’ve got what it takes, you’ll soon be playing an essential role in major projects, too.
* All. These. Benefits. Flexible hours, remote working, unlimited backing for learning and training, top-of-the-market health insurance, a rich relocation package, generous parental support, and a yearly retreat to a stunning location. We help each Spooner set up the conditions to do their best work.
* Competitive pay and access to company equity at a discount. Typically, we offer individuals with limited experience an annual salary of $204,281 in the United States. For candidates we assess as possessing exceptional potential and highly unusual achievement, compensation typically ranges $257,642 to $522,120. Compensation varies by location and expected impact. In higher-cost markets such as New York City, offers are generally positioned toward the upper end of the range. As you grow your expertise and increase your contributions, your compensation can grow rapidly alongside your impact.

**The selection process**
-------------------------

In our screening process, we prioritize verifiable signals of excellence, regardless of seniority. There are no preferential paths beyond what your application demonstrates, and we evaluate every candidate through the same process. Some people hold back because they feel they lack experience or have an “imperfect” CV. If you like the role and believe you could excel over time, don’t self-reject. All applications go through our careers page, which is the only way to be considered. If you pass our screening, you’ll be asked to complete one or more tests. They are challenging, may involve unfamiliar problems, and can take several hours. To learn more about what to expect throughout the selection process, you can find additional information here. We set the bar high and won’t extend an offer until we’re confident we’ve found the right candidate. This is why a job may remain open for months or be reposted several times. We consider all applicants for employment and provide reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities—please let us know through this form.

**Before you apply**
--------------------

If you’ve applied before but didn’t receive an offer, we recommend waiting at least one year before applying again.

Bending Spoons is a demanding environment. We’re extremely ambitious and we hold ourselves—and one another—to a high standard. While this tends to lead to extraordinary learning, achievement, and career growth, it also requires significant commitment.

To help you ramp up quickly and set yourself up for success, we expect you to spend most days in our Milan office during your first few months with us, regardless of your long-term work location. It’s the best way to rapidly absorb our company culture and build trust with your new teammates. We’ll support you with generous travel and accommodation assistance. After that, you’re welcome to work from one of our offices, or remotely from approved countries—depending on what we agree at the offer stage.

If the role speaks to you and you’re excited to give your best, we’d love to hear from you. Apply now—we can’t wait to meet you.

title: Director, Trade Marketing(LRP/Vichy)
description:
**Job Description:** Director Trade Marketing (LDB)
  
**Job Title:** Director, Trade Marketing
  
**Division:** L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty (LDB)
  
**Reports To:** AVP, Trade Marketing
  
  
**Location:** Hudson Yards, NY
  
  
Who We Are
  
  
The Trade Marketing team at L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty (LDB) operates as the critical commercial engine and strategic bridge between our world-class brands—CeraVe, La Roche-Posay, and Vichy—and our retail partners. We do not simply execute plans; we are the architects of the commercial strategy. We translate high-level national brand visions into concrete, localized, and winning trade architectures that dictate how our portfolio dominates at the shelf and on the screen.
  
  
We are looking for a powerhouse leader to step into the role of AVP, Trade Marketing. This is not a role for those who seek the path of least resistance. It is a high-visibility, high-stakes position that requires an individual with exceptional grit, an unshakeable work ethic, and a commanding professional presence. You will lead the charge in bridging marketing ambition with commercial reality, serving as a highly reliable, deeply trusted partner to both internal teams and retail giants.
  
  
The Opportunity & Your Impact
  
  
As the AVP of Trade Marketing, you will lead a high-performing team tasked with translating each brand's national strategy and defining the overarching commercial strategy for the division. You will be the ultimate owner of how CeraVe, La Roche-Posay, and Vichy show up commercially, establishing the promotional guardrails, trade spending efficiency parameters, and go-to-market execution plans.
  
  
This role demands a leader who is not afraid to go toe-to-toe with General Managers, Brand Presidents, and Marketing heads. You will be the voice of commercial reality, backed by bulletproof, data-driven analytics. When tough conversations are needed regarding how national strategies must adapt to the retail landscape, or when commercial parameters must be strictly defined, you will lean in with confidence, facts, and a solution-oriented attitude.
  
  
**What We’re Looking For:** Our Future Leader
  
  
We are searching for a relentless driver who brings a masterclass balance of strategic marketing translation, commercial street-smarts, and analytic rigor. You are someone who:
  

* Is a Strategic Translator: You can look at a national brand marketing plan and immediately identify how to operationalize it into a commercial strategy that retailers buy into.
* Possesses Deep Grit: You roll up your sleeves, thrive in fast-paced complexity, and view obstacles as puzzles to be solved. You are resilient, reliable, and run toward challenges, not away from them.
* Commands the Room: You have a strong, authentic leadership style and an executive presence that immediately builds trust.
* Engages in Constructive Friction: You are comfortable speaking truth to power. You are fearless in challenging GMs, Sales leaders, and Marketers to ensure our trade strategies are both commercially sound and highly profitable.
* Is Rooted in Data: Your opinions are strong, but they are always backed by objective, meticulous analytics. You are a trusted source of truth because you let the data do the heavy lifting.

Key Job Responsibilities
  

* Define Commercial Strategy for one of our two mass brands: Serve as the chief architect in translating brand-specific national strategies into a unified, high-performing divisional commercial strategy across all key retail channels.
* Translate National Brand Ambition: Act as the strategic conduit between Brand Marketing and Sales. Take national campaigns and product launches and translate them into commercially viable retail programs for CeraVe, La Roche-Posay, and Vichy.
* Commercial Guardrail Ownership: Establish and enforce rigorous divisional trade guidelines. Collaborate cross-functionally (Divisional Leadership, Sales, Marketing, and Finance) to align brand ambitions with commercial realities and strict ROI parameters.
* Fearless Stakeholder Management: Act as the strategic partner and challenger to GMs and Brand Teams. Drive the tough, necessary alignments on promotional ROI, pricing executions, and commercial trade spend when national strategies clash with field realities.
* Bulletproof Analytical Storytelling: Translate complex retailer, consumer, and financial data into clear, persuasive strategic narratives. Deliver high-impact presentations to executive leadership.
* Team Leadership & Capability Building: Lead, mentor, and inspire a high-performing Trade Marketing team, fostering a culture of high performance, accountability, and continuous development.
* P&L and ROI Optimization: Maintain a deep, precise understanding of the divisional P&L. Rigorously analyze promotional ROI and trade spend efficiency to identify and capture profit-improvement opportunities.
* Retailer & Field Collaboration: Work hand-in-hand with Field Sales and Customer Marketing to ensure our defined commercial plans are flawlessly executed, highly competitive, and customized to win across the retailer landscape.

Background & Experience Requirements
  
  
**Educational Background:**  

* Bachelor’s degree in Sales, Commercial Strategy, Marketing, Commercial Finance, Data Analytics, Economics, or a related business field. MBA is a plus.

**Professional Experience & Technical Skills:**  

* 7-12+ years of experience working in a fast-paced FMCG or CPG organization, with a strong preference for deep exposure to Trade Marketing, Commercial Strategy, or Category Management.
* Experienced managerial skills with multiple direct reports and upscaling junior talent
* Strategic Translation Track Record: Proven experience taking high-level brand ideas/national strategies and successfully mapping them into commercial, retailer-facing programs.
* Proven Leadership: A track record of leading teams and directly influencing senior, multi-functional leadership.
* Commercial Acumen: A deep understanding of the US retailer landscape, trade spend mechanics, and how brand marketing strategies translate to the retail shelf.
* Financial Literacy: Strong command of product financial structures and P&L dynamics; capability to evaluate the financial health of trade investments.
* Analytical Rigor: Hands-on experience working with large, complex datasets to derive actionable insights. Familiarity with syndicated data sources (Circana/IRI, Numerator, Nielsen) and trade promotion management tools.
* Technical Proficiency: High comfort level with data visualization and analytics tools (Advanced Excel, Power BI, Tableau) to build data-backed arguments.

**Salary range:** $138K-$200K

title: Chief Operating Officer
description:
**Shape the Next Chapter of Achievement First**
-----------------------------------------------

What does it take to make 41 schools work exceptionally well, every day, while rebuilding the systems that support them? Achievement First is seeking a Chief Operating Officer who can bring simplicity to complexity, set a high bar for operational execution, and lead the work of building a stronger, more integrated network. This is an opportunity for an executive who finds purpose in demanding, consequential work and knows how to turn operational challenges into lasting institutional strength.

**The Opportunity**
-------------------

Founded in 1999, Achievement First Public Charter Schools is a nonprofit network of 41 public charter schools serving approximately 15,000 students across Connecticut, New York, and Rhode Island. Our mission is to prepare every student to excel in college and career, deepen their knowledge of self and community, and lead lives of purpose. In partnership with families and communities, we work to disrupt the legacy of inequity in education and believe deeply in the unlimited potential of every student.

Achievement First is renewing academic excellence through a redesign of its K–12 instructional program. At the same time, the environment for public education is changing: families have evolving expectations and more options, and schools must deliver compelling experiences while managing cost, regulation, facilities, and technology. Internally, the network's growth outpaced the development of some central systems and shared operating practices, leaving uneven processes and insufficiently codified standards. AF has recently moved to a more decentralized model in which Regional Executive Directors lead regional academics and operations, and the COO sets networkwide standards and drives consistent performance through strong functional leadership and regional partnership.

The COO reports to the Chief Executive Officer and serves on the Executive Leadership Team. The role owns a portfolio spanning facilities and real estate, school operations support, student enrollment, operational risk, and Information, Technology, and Data, with an approximately $45 million budget, 4 direct reports and 42 positions. Regional executives retain direct authority over regional operations teams, so the COO leads through shared standards, clear performance expectations, and defined executive and regional decision channels. The next COO will inherit real strengths to build upon, alongside work that needs to be simplified, codified, and redesigned. This leader will set the operating vision, make disciplined choices about internal capability and external partnerships, and will turn fragmented practices into reliable, repeatable systems without losing momentum in schools.

The opportunity is demanding and consequential: enables the daily experience of students and educators while building the operational bedrock for durable performance and future scale. Achievement First needs a leader energized by creating a clear path where there is ambiguity, capable of making hard tradeoffs, and skilled at bringing people on the change journey. Success will depend on the ability to own results, lead specialized experts and vendors, challenge colleagues, and create coherence across a complex organization.

**What You Will Lead**
----------------------

### **Create Exceptional School Environments**

Set and implement the vision and standards for school environments across the network. Own performance expectations for facilities and essential services, and establish the reviews, escalation mechanisms, and actions that keep schools safe, welcoming, and ready, creating an environment that facilitates learning.

### **Strengthen Operational Systems and Organizational Alignment**

Lead the design and implementation of common operational standards, processes, and accountability mechanisms. Set clear network expectations with Regional Executive Directors, define practical decision and escalation paths, and drive adoption of repeatable processes. Ensure operational changes enable the redesigned K–12 instructional program and maintain service continuity during implementation.

Own performance across a portfolio of 29 school facilities and two offices, including maintenance, capital projects, facilities strategy, and long-range real estate planning. title: Senior Partnerships Manager
description:
### **About Oath**

Oath is the strategic giving platform designed to help donors maximize the impact of their contributions by guiding them to the races and causes where their dollars can make the greatest impact. Oath has directed over $150M while protecting donors' data and avoiding the spam and spin of other giving platforms. As the one stop shop for a generation of donors who want to make a difference, Oath is building the future of philanthropy.

The Partnerships team owns Oath's relationships with the organizations that move money at scale: PACs, donor networks, party committees, and bundlers. Partners use Oath to direct their giving to the races that matter most, and we make it better, faster, and smarter. This role leads that team into the 2028 presidential cycle.

### **The Opportunity**

You'll lead Oath's strategy for organizational partners, one of our three growth pillars. Your mission is to grow partner-driven giving for 2028 by signing, growing, and retaining the organizations whose members want to give strategically. Most 2028 partner agreements will be signed in 2027. You'll own that strategy: who we partner with, what we offer them, how we credit their results, and how we keep them coming back cycle after cycle. This role combines business development with account leadership and reporting. You'll have the autonomy to set strategy, shape the partner offering, and grow the team.

### **Key Responsibilities**

* Own the partnerships strategy end-to-end: Set the partner strategy, target list, and calendar, aligned to Oath's priorities and the 2028 cycle
* Build the pipeline and close new partners: Identify, pitch, and close PACs, donor collectives, party committees, and progressive organizations
* Own the enterprise offer: Set pricing, fee-for-service terms, co-branded packages, and reporting commitments
* Deliver partner reporting: Use internal systems and AI to deliver accurate reports that show each partner the donations their work drove
* Report, measure, and iterate: Build and own pipeline, revenue, retention, and partner-driven giving reporting.
* Partner cross-functionally: Bring partner needs to Product so the platform serves organizations as well as individual donors. Ensure alignment between partnerships, marketing, and product roadmap

  
**Requirements**  

* + 6+ years in partnerships, business development, or sales, including at least 3 years managing teams
  + Proven track record closing and growing sales accounts, with numbers to show for it
  + Ownership mindset: comfortable building processes and teams from scratch and iterating quickly
  + Data-literate: can read and build dashboards, question an attribution model, and explain results in plain language
  + Ideally a working knowledge of campaign finance rules, and the judgment to know when to call counsel
  + Mission-driven: genuine interest in progressive politics and donor engagement

  
**Benefits**  

* Base Salary: $150k-$200k
* Equity package
* Health Insurance: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage
* Retirement: 401(k) matching
* Time Off: Flexible PTO
* Office: 3 days per week in our NYC headquarters; flexible remote work for the other 2 days

description:
**Who we are:**

For over 25 years, Global Relay has set the standard in enterprise information archiving with industry-leading cloud archiving, surveillance, eDiscovery, and analytics solutions. We securely capture and preserve the communications data of the world's most highly regulated firms, giving them greater visibility and control over their information and ensuring compliance with stringent regulations.

Though we offer competitive compensation and benefits and all the other perks one would expect from an established company, we are not your typical technology company. Global Relay is a career-building company. A place for big ideas. New challenges. Groundbreaking innovation. It's a place where you can genuinely make an impact – and be recognized for it.

We believe great businesses thrive on diversity, inclusion, and the contributions of all employees. To that end, we recruit candidates from different backgrounds and foster a work environment that encourages employees to collaborate and learn from each other, completely free of barriers.

**Your Role**

As Senior Manager, Customer Success Operations, you will lead the operational processes, insights and frameworks that enable our global Customer Success organisation to deliver customer value, protect recurring revenue and scale effectively.

Supporting approximately 50 Customer Success professionals, you will partner closely with the Chief Customer Officer and Global Head of Sales Operations to strengthen customer engagement, renewals and account growth. You will translate business priorities into practical processes, reliable reporting and clear accountability across the post-sales customer lifecycle.

This is a hands-on leadership role combining strategic planning with operational delivery. You will lead a geographically distributed team and partner with Customer Success, Sales, Finance and Product to support an increasingly complex enterprise customer base.

**Your Responsibilities**

**Renewal Strategy and Revenue Protection**

* Build a proactive renewal operating model with clear milestones, ownership and escalation routes ahead of contract expiry.
* Support the transition from reactive auto-renewals to planned, strategic renewal discussions, including multi-year agreements where appropriate.
* Establish visibility into upcoming renewals, customer risk, contraction and expansion opportunities.
* Partner with Customer Success and Finance to improve renewal forecasting and explain revenue movements.
* Develop consistent reporting on MRR, ARR, gross revenue retention, net revenue retention and churn.

**Contract Reconciliation Billing and True Ups**

* Own the operational coordination of contract reconciliations and true-ups, partnering with Finance and account owners to ensure accurate, timely billing.
* Identify differences between contractual commitments, customer usage, entitlements and billing records.
* Investigate recurring discrepancies and introduce controls that reduce revenue leakage and customer friction.
* Ensure reconciliation decisions, exceptions and approvals are documented and traceable.

**Customer Engagement and Lifecycle Management**

* Develop a consistent engagement framework across onboarding, adoption, ongoing account management and renewal.
* Define account segmentation and coverage models that align CS resources with customer needs, complexity and commercial value.
* Set clear expectations for customer touchpoints, account plans, business reviews and risk escalation.
* Develop customer health scoring using product adoption, engagement, support and commercial indicators; measure effectiveness against customer outcomes.

**Data Systems and Performance Insights**

* Establish a reliable view of customer and revenue performance, with clear metric definitions and ownership.
* Build dashboards that help leaders identify risks, prioritise activity and assess team effectiveness.
* Partner with systems owners to improve CRM data quality, workflow automation and reporting consistency.
* Translate complex data into clear recommendations and simplify manual processes to improve scalability.

**Team Leadership and Cross Functional Delivery**

* Lead, coach and develop the London-based Manager and Vancouver-based Analyst.
* Set priorities and balance day-to-day operational requirements with longer-term improvement initiatives.
* Establish effective working practices across New York, London and Vancouver.
* Build partnerships across Customer Success, Sales, Finance and Product to resolve issues and deliver shared priorities.
* Lead process changes through clear communication, practical training and measurement of adoption.

**About You**

You are an experienced Customer Success Operations, Revenue Operations or post-sales operations professional who combines commercial understanding with strong analytical and operational skills. You bring structure to complex environments and move comfortably between executive discussions and detailed problem-solving.

* Demonstrated experience leading Customer Success Operations or a comparable post-sales operations function within an enterprise SaaS business.
* Strong understanding of onboarding, adoption, renewals, retention and expansion.
* Financial and commercial acumen, including SaaS revenue metrics, billing, contract reconciliation and true ups.
* Experience building renewal processes, engagement frameworks, account segmentation and customer health models.
* Strong analytical skills and experience using CRM platforms, reporting tools and workflows to improve data quality and effectiveness.
* People management experience, including developing colleagues and coordinating delivery across locations and time zones.
* Confidence partnering with senior leaders, presenting recommendations and constructively challenging existing approaches.
* A hands-on approach, sound judgement and the ability to prioritise competing demands in a fast-paced environment.
* Experience supporting financial services customers, regulated industries or complex enterprise contracts would be advantageous.

title: Associate Manager, Accounting (Hybrid)
description:
With millions of diners, 70,000+ restaurant partners and 25+ years of experience, OpenTable, part of Booking Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: BKNG), is an industry leader with a passion for helping restaurants thrive. Our world-class technology empowers restaurants to focus on what matters most – their team, their guests, and their bottom line – while enabling diners to discover and book the perfect restaurant for every occasion.

Every employee at OpenTable has a tangible impact on what we do and how we do it. You'll also be part of a global team and its portfolio of metasearch brands. Hospitality is all about taking care of others, and it defines our culture.

**About The Job**

OpenTable is looking for an Associate Manager, Accounting to own a highly technical portfolio spanning partnership revenue, loyalty, and leases, along with other technical areas such as bad debt, prepaids, and accruals, and the close-related operations that support them. The role sits at the intersection of technical accounting, revenue recognition, contract interpretation, and cross-functional business partnership.

This is an Associate Manager–level individual contributor role with significant ownership and influence: you'll lead complex workstreams, coach teammates, streamline processes, and work cross-functionally to support business partners. It's built for someone with strong judgment and technical depth who can navigate the organization independently, lead day-to-day execution, communicate plan and progress clearly, and improve how the work gets done. This role reports to the Manager, Accounting. This posting is for an existing vacancy.

**Responsibilities**

* Own the end-to-end accounting for fast-growing strategic partnership revenue programs, managing complex models to support revenue and expense recognition and balance sheet treatment
* Own the technical accounting for the evolving loyalty program, using judgment to evaluate the key assumptions that drive it
* Lead the accounting across other technical areas including leases, bad debt, prepaids, and accruals, spanning multiple OpenTable legal entities, all reported under US GAAP
* Manage close-related accounting activities, including journal entries, reconciliations, and balance sheet integrity across these areas
* Organize and lead cross-functional workstreams, building strong, productive working relationships with stakeholders across the company — including teammates and partners in Finance, Product, Legal, Sales, Strategy, Operations, and AP
* Prepare clear technical accounting memos and documentation, support internal controls, and walk internal and external auditors through positions and supporting evidence
* Drive process improvements that reduce manual work and help the team scale, through stronger process design, system connectivity, and AI-enabled workflows

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
* 6+ years of progressive accounting experience with deep knowledge of US GAAP, including operationalizing guidance for revenue recognition (ASC 606) and lease accounting (ASC 842).
* CPA certification or equivalent technical accounting depth.
* Advanced Excel proficiency, including extensive experience with complex financial modeling, lookups, and pivot tables.
* Demonstrated analytical, communication, and stakeholder-management skills with the ability to collaborate across technical and non-technical teams.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in public accounting or professional financial services.
* Proficiency with NetSuite or similar enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems.

title: Italian Sourcing Analyst

Job Summary

Roman's is seeking a detail-oriented and analytical Italian Sourcing Analyst to support supplier research, sourcing strategies, purchasing decisions, and cost analysis for ingredients, food products, and operational supplies. This role focuses on identifying reliable suppliers, evaluating product quality and pricing, analyzing market trends, and helping maintain an efficient and cost-effective sourcing process.

The ideal candidate has strong research, analytical, and communication skills, along with an interest in Italian cuisine, specialty ingredients, or food supply operations. The successful applicant will collaborate with purchasing, operations, finance, and inventory teams to assess sourcing opportunities, maintain supplier records, and support informed procurement decisions.

Key Responsibilities

* Research and identify potential suppliers of Italian food ingredients, specialty products, packaging, and operational materials.
* Analyze supplier pricing, product specifications, availability, quality standards, and delivery capabilities.
* Compare supplier proposals and prepare reports to support sourcing and purchasing decisions.
* Collect and evaluate market information related to ingredient costs, availability, and supply trends.
* Assist with developing sourcing strategies that balance cost, quality, reliability, and operational requirements.
* Maintain accurate supplier databases, product catalogs, quotations, and sourcing documentation.
* Coordinate with purchasing teams to review procurement requirements and prioritize sourcing activities.
* Monitor supplier performance, including delivery reliability, product consistency, responsiveness, and pricing.
* Support supplier negotiations by preparing cost comparisons and relevant market research.
* Identify alternative suppliers and products to help reduce supply risks and prevent shortages.
* Review ingredient specifications and coordinate quality-related questions with relevant teams.
* Track changes in market prices and communicate potential cost impacts to management.
* Help assess sourcing risks, including seasonal availability, lead times, and supplier capacity.
* Prepare spreadsheets, summaries, and presentations covering sourcing costs and supplier evaluations.
* Collaborate with inventory and operations teams to align sourcing decisions with demand and stock requirements.
* Recommend improvements to sourcing procedures, supplier selection, and procurement efficiency.

Qualifications and Requirements

* Bachelor's degree in supply chain management, business, economics, finance, analytics, or a related field preferred.
* Previous experience in sourcing, procurement, purchasing analysis, market research, or supply chain operations is an advantage.
* Strong analytical and research skills.
* Proficiency with spreadsheets and standard business software.
* Ability to organize supplier information and interpret pricing data accurately.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Excellent attention to detail and documentation practices.
* Ability to manage multiple research assignments and deadlines.
* Professional approach to supplier communication and cross-functional teamwork.
* Understanding of purchasing processes, supplier evaluation, and cost analysis.

Preferred Skills

* Experience sourcing food ingredients, specialty Italian products, restaurant supplies, or consumer goods.
* Familiarity with Italian ingredients, including pasta, cheeses, olive oils, tomatoes, herbs, and specialty products.
* Knowledge of supplier assessment, quotation comparisons, and procurement documentation.
* Experience with inventory systems, purchasing platforms, or enterprise resource planning software.
* Ability to use data to identify cost-saving opportunities and sourcing risks.
* Understanding of food quality specifications, traceability, and applicable sourcing requirements.
* Italian language skills may be beneficial when communicating with Italian suppliers.

Work Environment

The Italian Sourcing Analyst generally works in an office or business operations setting, collaborating with purchasing, finance, inventory, and supplier management teams. The role involves research, data analysis, documentation, and regular communication with internal stakeholders and external suppliers. Occasional supplier visits or product evaluations may be required depending on business needs.

* Opportunities to develop analytical, sourcing, and procurement skills.
* Exposure to supplier research and supply chain decision-making.
* Collaborative and professional working environment.
* Potential career advancement into strategic sourcing, procurement management, or supply chain analysis.

* Additional benefits may be available according to company policy.

Roman's is the company named for this employment opportunity. The Italian Sourcing Analyst will support sourcing and purchasing activities by researching suppliers, evaluating product options, analyzing costs, and maintaining accurate sourcing information. This role is suited to an analytical professional who values supplier reliability, product quality, and efficient business operations.

Interested candidates should submit a resume highlighting relevant experience in sourcing, procurement, market research, business analysis, or supply chain operations. The Drug Intelligence and Intervention Group (DIIG) at OCME was created for the joint purposes of:
  
  
1. Tracking suspected and confirmed overdose deaths,
  
  
2. Providing public sector leaders with timely and actionable information about fatal overdose, and
  
  
3. Providing direct support to family and friends of overdose victims in NYC.
  
  
DIIG conducts public health surveillance of overdose, collecting and leveraging data before and after OCME has determined cause and manner of death. Towards this end, DIIG is responsible for timely and accurate identification of suspected overdose cases and monitoring and reporting overdose trends. DIIG also plans and facilitates inter-agency collaboration through a citywide initiative called RxStat by planning and hosting monthly interdisciplinary meetings on overdose prevention. These RxStat meetings, including the quarterly OCME-led Overdose Fatality Review meeting, are attended by representatives from over 30 different local, state, and federal agencies.
  
  
The Data and Surveillance Supervisor is responsible for overseeing the long-term planning and management of multiple large scale data systems improvement projects for the Drug Intelligence and
  
Intervention Group. They will work closely with OCME colleagues, research partners, and other city agencies to identify opportunities for greater efficiency, timeliness, and accuracy of data sharing, analysis, and reporting related to overdose and DIIG engagement with overdose bereaved individuals. This position will report to the DIIG Deputy Director and work closely with OCME IT to ensure DIIG data capture and analysis processes are integrated into agency operations appropriately and with sustainability in mind.
  
  
The Data and Surveillance Supervisor will:
  
  
Lead and supervise a team of epidemiologists, data analysts, and support staff in the collection, management, and analysis of overdose-related data.
  
  
Oversee the design, implementation, and maintenance of data systems to improve overdose mortality surveillance and reporting.
  
  
Develop strategic vision for enhancing data infrastructure, including implementing new technologies and methodologies for more efficient data capture and analysis.
  
  
Champion data quality improvement initiatives, including standardization of protocols, validation procedures, and quality control systems.
  
  
Manage relationships with external partners including law enforcement agencies, public health agencies, and academic institutions.
  
  
Lead the development of dashboards and visualization tools to communicate mortality data to stakeholders and the public.
  
  
Ensure compliance with legal, ethical, and regulatory standards for death investigation data and protected health information.
  
  
Spearhead innovative approaches to identifying emerging overdose trends through mortality data analytics.
  
  
Translate complex epidemiological findings into actionable recommendations for overdose prevention interventions and public policy.
  
  
Serve as a subject matter expert for research partnerships, providing expert consultation on study design, statistical analysis, and data interpretation.

**Accenture Flex** offers you the flexibility of local fixed-duration project-based work powered by Accenture, a leading global professional services company. Accenture is consistently recognized on FORTUNE's 100 Best Companies to Work For and Diversity Inc's Top 50 Companies For Diversity lists.

As an **Accenture Flex** employee, you will apply your skills and experience to help drive business transformation for leading organizations and communities. In addition to delivering innovative solutions for Accenture's clients, you will work with a highly skilled, diverse network of people across Accenture businesses who are using the latest emerging technologies to address today's biggest business challenges.

You will receive competitive rewards and access to benefits programs and world-class learning resources. **Accenture Flex** employees work in their local metro area onsite at the project, significantly reducing and/or eliminating the demands to travel.

**Key Responsibilities:**

  

* As a Scrum Master, you will be responsible for enabling the effective functioning of a software development team using Agile methodologies.
* Your day-to-day activities will include coaching and mentoring the Scrum Team or Teams, removing obstacles that hinder progress, and facilitating Agile ceremonies such as sprint planning, daily stand ups, sprint reviews, and retrospectives.
* You will also identify and report progress through appropriate metrics.
* You are expected to be a subject matter expert, collaborate and manage the team to perform effectively, take responsibility for team decisions, engage with multiple teams, contribute to key decisions, and provide solutions to problems within your immediate team and across multiple teams.
* Promote continuous improvement by identifying opportunities to enhance team performance and Agile practices.
* Facilitate clear communication and collaboration among team members and stakeholders to ensure alignment on project goals.
* Support the resolution of conflicts and challenges within the team to maintain a productive and positive work environment.
* Analyze project metrics and feedback to drive data informed decisions and improve delivery outcomes.
* Champion Agile values and principles across the organization to foster a culture of adaptability and innovation.

**Note:** role requires 3 days per week onsite client work and client mandated time away 5 days per quarter

  

**Basic Qualifications:**

* 7+ years of experience in Agile delivery, Scrum Master, or Business Analyst roles
* 3+ years of hands-on experience as a Scrum Master facilitating Scrum ceremonies for teams of 15+ members
* 3+ years of experience with SAFe (working with RTEs, PMO, and Product Owners; PI/quarterly planning)
* Strong experience in requirements elicitation, writing user stories, and defining acceptance criteria
* Proficiency with JIRA and Confluence; working knowledge of ALM Octane or a similar test management tool
* Working knowledge of SQL and data analysis
* Experience with Agile metrics (velocity, burndown/burnup, cycle time, lead time)
* Experience supporting UAT and collaborating with QA teams
* Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills
* Bachelor's Degree

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Certified SAFe Scrum Master (SSM) or Certified AI-Empowered SAFe Scrum Master; CSM or PSM also valued
* Experience in the financial services or banking domain, especially fraud detection, prevention, or fraud claims
* Hands-on experience with generative AI tools (GitHub Copilot with Jira integration, Microsoft Copilot, DevEx Plan) and prompt engineering for Agile artifacts
* Experience with process modeling tools and notation (UML, MS Visio)
* Technical background in databases (Oracle, MS SQL Server, T-SQL) and familiarity with REST APIs and messaging platforms (Kafka, IBM MQ)
* Experience working across 8+ Agile Release Trains in a large-scale SAFe environment
* Prior experience as a Business Analyst or software developer
